result.summary: This PR replaces the maintainer-run Python script that precomputes headers-sync DoS-protection parameters (commitment period, redownload buffer size) with a runtime C++ computation done at node startup, based on the chain's age and minimum-chainwork height. It adds a closed-form optimizer with unit and fuzz tests, and deletes the now-unused contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py script and its release-process instructions. Mid-review, a reviewer found the underlying attack model (inherited from the old Python script) slightly underestimated attacker capability, and the author rewrote the algorithm to drop the batching assumption entirely, at a modest per-peer memory cost.
result.problem: Maintainers currently have to periodically re-run an external script and manually paste new constants into chainparams for every release, and that process was shown to slightly mis-model the attack it defends against. This wastes maintainer time and risks shipping parameters that are stale or subtly wrong, which affects the DoS protection all users get during headers sync.

open_concerns: darosior's finding that the attack_rate routine may still underestimate the rate for incomplete final batches, which prompted the full rewrite now on the PR - not yet re-reviewed.

shuv-amp's earlier report of ComputeHeadersSyncParams hanging for small minchainwork_headers combined with short timespan was fixed by the author with a non-strict comparison and extra Assume() guards.
resolved_concerns: ajtowns's question about whether NodeClock::now() feeding into parameter selection could leak information; sipa investigated and found the parameters only change every ~22 days and the leak is minor, judged acceptable.
shuv-amp's int/int64_t mismatch for next_height was fixed in a follow-up commit.
darosior's several nits on comment clarity in headerssync.cpp are minor and non-blocking.

result.card: This PR moves the headers-sync DoS-protection tuning parameters (commitment period, redownload buffer size) from values precomputed by a maintainer-run Python script into a runtime C++ computation based on chain age and minchainwork height, removing a recurring manual release step. During review, darosior found the underlying attack model (inherited from the old script) underestimated what an attacker sending a short final header batch could achieve, and the author rewrote the algorithm to drop the batching assumption entirely, at the cost of roughly 14.7 KiB more per-peer memory. Concept ACKs came from sedited, darosior and fjahr, and an approach ACK from ajtowns, with no standing objection to the new approach, though it has not yet had a fresh review pass since the 2026-09-15/16 rewrite. It also deletes the now-obsolete contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py script and trims the release-process doc that referenced it. The PR conflicts with two other open PRs (#35474, #35301) touching overlapping files.
